Mast Trail was mostly well-maintained and good nature vibes for a moderate hike with lots of ups and downs. Vista Trail was closed after the viewpoint. There was an unmaintained alternative trail on the side shown on AllTrails, but there were a lot of weeds and they were very tall. There was not much to see at Cedar Trail as there were tall weeds on both sides of the trail. Orchard Trail was maintained and surroundings were ok, but had a LOT of bugs. Overall the trail felt a bit outdated, and quite a few sections were closed so needed to detour a few too many times.

This trail is absolutely amazing. There is plenty of free parking available in the main parking lot at 1749 Meadowvale Rd, Toronto, ON M1B 5W8. The walking terrain is flat mostly without any rocks. There is good elevation which could challenge your body. The only downside was that even though this is a long trail but there are no washrooms on the trail.

Great Hike that gives a glimpse of the Rouge Park. Lots of people including runners. We started from the Twyne River Parking lot which has ample space. Went Northwards on Orchard Trail. Reached the pond with railway tracks running on the east side. Saw a Heron there. Crossed the paved Road and moved into Cedar Trail. The southern portion has a marsh with many turtles. Kept going northward on Cedar Trail and crossed the Little Rouge Creek - which actually crisscrosses the hiking path several times. The reason why this is called Orchard Trail becomes obvious once you enter the Cedar Forest. This trail sees a steep gradient with a stairway. Returned back and hiked through the Vista Trail. The platform on Vista Trail is great.

All this while we never ever saw the Rouge River. For that you have to hike the portions South of the Twyne River Lot on the Mast Trail.  

Walking from the Vista Platform to the Twyne Road is great as it is a walk on the Ridge. This carries through on the South Side of Twyne Road on the Mast Trail. 

Ran out of time half way into Mast Trail and returned back to parking. Did get to see the Rouge River. Much greater flow than the Little Rouge.
